about_intro: Jiyuu (自由, “freedom”) is a small social network for short posts. You can write posts, follow people, and like and comment on what they share.
about_origin: Jiyuu started as a project for our Japanese class. We're building it as if it were a real public social network, and our classmates and teachers are its first users.
about_team: JIYUU Team, a team of five students. Each of us owns one part of the app, from sign-in and profiles to feeds, notifications, and search.
about_tech: Jiyuu is built with {#sveltekit}SvelteKit{/sveltekit}, runs on {#cloudflare}Cloudflare{/cloudflare} Workers with a Cloudflare D1 database, and uses {#better_auth}Better Auth{/better_auth} for sign-in. The source code is public on {#github}GitHub{/github}.
about_contact: Found a bug or have an idea? Open an issue on {#issues}GitHub{/issues}. For anything else, email {#email}jiyuu.org@gmail.com{/email}.
terms_intro: By using Jiyuu, you agree to these terms. Jiyuu is a student project run by JIYUU Team.
terms_account: You sign in with your Google account, so keep it secure. You're responsible for what happens while you're signed in. Use one account per person, and don't pretend to be someone else.
terms_age: You must be at least 13 years old to use Jiyuu.
terms_age_note: The team hasn't decided on a minimum age. 13 is a common default.
terms_content: You own what you post, photos included. By posting, you let Jiyuu store it and show it to other people. Only upload photos you took or have the right to share, and don’t post other people’s personal information, such as where they live, without their permission. You can delete your posts at any time.
terms_content_sources: GIFs come from GIPHY and are covered by {#giphy_terms}GIPHY’s terms{/giphy_terms}. Place names come from {#osm}OpenStreetMap{/osm} (© OpenStreetMap contributors).
terms_rule_hate: post hate speech, or violent or sexual content
terms_rule_illegal: break the law, or share things you don't have the right to share
terms_rule_spam: spam, or try to break or overload the service
terms_enforcement: We may remove content or suspend accounts that break these rules.
terms_service: Jiyuu is provided as is, without any warranty. Because it's a student project, features can change, data can be reset, and the service may shut down for any reason.
terms_liability: As far as the law allows, the Jiyuu team isn't liable for any loss that comes from using Jiyuu.
terms_law: These terms are governed by the laws of Cambodia.
terms_law_note: The team hasn't chosen a governing law yet.
terms_changes: We may update these terms. The date at the top shows when they last changed. If you keep using Jiyuu after a change, you accept the new terms.
privacy_intro: This policy explains what Jiyuu collects when you use it, why, and what you can do about it. Jiyuu is run by JIYUU Team, a student team.
privacy_collect_google: When you sign in with Google: your name, email address, and profile photo, plus your Google account ID and the sign-in tokens Google issues. We never see your Google password.
privacy_collect_session: While you're signed in: a session record with its expiry time, your IP address, and your browser's user agent. Our sign-in system keeps these to secure your session.
privacy_collect_content: What you share: your profile (username, display name, bio, profile photo, and banner), your posts and the photos, GIFs, polls, and places you add to them, comments, likes, poll votes, and who you follow.
privacy_collect_photos: Photos you upload, for posts or your profile: before storing a photo, we remove its hidden metadata, such as where it was taken (GPS location), the camera or phone and its serial number, and editing details. We keep only which way up the photo goes, so it isn’t shown sideways.
privacy_collect_places: Places: a post shows a place only when you pick one from the place search. Jiyuu never reads your device’s location.
privacy_use: Only to run Jiyuu: to sign you in, show your profile and posts, and notify you inside the app. We don't sell your data, show ads, or use analytics or tracking tools.
privacy_public: You have to sign in to see anything on Jiyuu, so your profile, posts, comments, likes, and follows are visible only to signed-in users. That includes the photos, GIFs, and places you add to posts. Anyone with a Google account can sign up, though, so treat what you post as visible to the whole Jiyuu community. Polls show only vote totals: we store your vote so you can’t vote twice, but Jiyuu never shows anyone who voted for what. Other users never see your email address.
privacy_cookies_intro: Jiyuu only sets cookies it needs to work:
privacy_cookie_session: a session cookie that keeps you signed in, removed when you log out or the session expires
privacy_cookie_state: a cookie that protects the Google sign-in step and expires after 5 minutes
privacy_cookie_locale: a cookie that remembers the language you picked, for up to 400 days
privacy_storage_emoji: The emoji picker also saves the emoji list and your recently used emoji in your browser’s storage. That data stays on your device.
privacy_providers: Google handles sign-in and Cloudflare hosts the app and its database. Their own policies cover the data they handle: see {#google}Google's privacy policy{/google} and {#cloudflare_privacy}Cloudflare's privacy policy{/cloudflare_privacy}.
privacy_providers_giphy: GIFs come from GIPHY. Your GIF searches reach GIPHY through our server, so they don’t carry your IP address, but GIFs load directly from GIPHY: opening the GIF picker or viewing a post with a GIF sends your IP address and browser details to GIPHY. See {#giphy_privacy}GIPHY’s privacy policy{/giphy_privacy}.
privacy_providers_places: Place search uses Photon by komoot, built on {#osm}OpenStreetMap{/osm} data. Only what you type is sent, through our server, never your IP address or location. We keep search results for a day to avoid repeat lookups, and they aren’t linked to your account. See {#komoot_privacy}komoot’s privacy policy{/komoot_privacy}.
privacy_providers_links: Link previews: when a post has a link, our server reads that page once to show its title, description and picture, and keeps a copy of the picture. Only the link is sent, never your IP address or account, and the site isn’t contacted when someone views the post.
privacy_providers_translate: “Translate post” sends the post’s text, through our server and never with your IP address or account, to {#deepl_privacy}DeepL{/deepl_privacy} for English and Japanese, or to Cloudflare Workers AI for Khmer. Each translation is saved so a post is translated only once. DeepL’s free service may keep text for a limited time to improve its translations, so posts from private accounts are only ever translated by Cloudflare.
privacy_providers_emoji: The emoji picker downloads its emoji list from jsDelivr, which receives your IP address and browser details. See {#jsdelivr_privacy}jsDelivr’s privacy policy{/jsdelivr_privacy}.
privacy_providers_github: The {#about}About page{/about} shows the team's profile photos, loaded from GitHub. Opening that page sends your IP address and browser details to GitHub. See {#github_privacy}GitHub's privacy statement{/github_privacy}.
privacy_retention: Your account and posts stay until you delete them or ask us to delete your account. Deleting a post deletes its photos, and so does removing a photo while you write or edit a post. If you close the page partway through writing a post, photos already uploaded for it can stay in storage; email us and we’ll remove them. A session expires about a week after you last use it.
privacy_rights: You can edit your profile and delete your posts and comments at any time. To get a copy of your data or delete your account, email {#email}jiyuu.org@gmail.com{/email}. Please don't put personal information in public GitHub issues.
privacy_children: Jiyuu isn't meant for children under 13, and we don't knowingly collect their data.
privacy_changes: If this policy changes, we'll update the date at the top of this page.
a11y_intro: We want everyone to be able to use Jiyuu, whatever device, language, or assistive technology they use.
a11y_goal: We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines ({#wcag}WCAG 2.2{/wcag}) at level AA.
a11y_goal_note: The team hasn't formally agreed on a conformance target.
a11y_done_semantic: Use real buttons, links, and headings, so keyboards and screen readers work as expected
a11y_done_labels: Label every form field and control, and describe profile pictures with alt text
a11y_done_focus: Show a visible outline on whatever has keyboard focus
a11y_done_theme: Offer light and dark themes that follow your device setting
a11y_done_lang: Offer the full interface in English, Japanese, and Khmer, and mark each page with its language so screen readers pronounce it correctly
a11y_done_responsive: Use layouts that work on screens from 360px-wide phones to desktops
a11y_done_photos: Let you reorder photos and move the crop box with the arrow keys as well as by dragging
a11y_done_alt: Let you describe each photo and GIF in a post with alt text, which screen readers read out. Without a description, photos are announced as “Photo 1 of 3” and GIFs as “Animated GIF”.
a11y_limit_audit: Jiyuu hasn't had a formal accessibility audit yet.
a11y_limit_google: Sign-in happens on Google's pages, which we don't control.
a11y_limit_translation: Native speakers are still reviewing the Japanese and Khmer text.
a11y_limit_gif_motion: GIFs play automatically and can’t be paused yet.
a11y_limit_crop_resize: Resizing the crop box needs a mouse or touch; the keyboard can only move it.
a11y_feedback: If something is hard to use, open an issue on {#issues}GitHub{/issues} or email {#email}jiyuu.org@gmail.com{/email}. Tell us the page, what you tried, and the device or assistive technology you use.

guidelines_intro: Jiyuu is a place for classmates and teachers to talk freely. These rules keep it that way. They apply to posts, replies, profiles, photos, links and direct messages.
guidelines_never_intro: Posting any of these gets the post removed and the account suspended at once.
guidelines_not_allowed_intro: Posts that do any of these are removed, and each removal is a strike against the account.
guidelines_sensitive: Artistic or educational nudity, newsworthy violence, medical photos and horror art may stay, blurred until someone chooses to see them. Mark such a post as sensitive yourself; a moderator may mark it too.
guidelines_allowed: Opinions, including criticism of the school or teachers, talking about your own feelings, and swearing that isn’t aimed at anyone are all fine.
guidelines_strike_warning: A first strike is a warning.
guidelines_strike_suspend: {strikes} strikes within {window} days suspend the account for {days} days.
guidelines_strike_ban: {strikes} strikes in all suspend the account permanently.
guidelines_strike_severe: Anything in “Never allowed” suspends the account at once, without strikes.
guidelines_checks: Posts are checked for spam and dangerous links when you send them, and English posts and photos are checked automatically for harmful content afterwards. An automatic check can blur or hide a post until a moderator looks at it, but only a moderator removes posts or suspends accounts. The text of direct messages is never read unless someone in the chat reports it.
guidelines_appeals_heading: If a moderator acts on your post or account
guidelines_appeals: You’re told which rule was broken. You can ask for a review of each decision once. A removed post is kept for one day so you can ask; if you do, it’s kept until the moderator decides. Otherwise it’s deleted for good, with its photos.
guidelines_contact: Questions about these rules go to {#email}jiyuu.org@gmail.com{/email}.
rule_child_safety_desc: Any sexual or sexualised image or text involving anyone under 18.
rule_threat_desc: Threatening to hurt a person, a school or a group of people.
rule_terrorism_desc: Recruiting for, praising or glorifying attacks on people.
rule_intimate_media_desc: Sharing private sexual images of someone, including fakes made of a real person.
rule_doxxing_desc: Someone else’s home address, phone number, ID or student number, or where they are.
rule_self_harm_encouragement_desc: Telling someone to hurt or kill themselves.
rule_hate_desc: Attacking people for their ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender, sexuality or disability.
rule_harassment_desc: Targeting one person again and again, or piling on in replies and mentions.
rule_impersonation_desc: Pretending to be a classmate, a teacher or an official account.
rule_spam_desc: Repeated or copied posts, mass mentions, mass following and ads.
rule_scam_desc: Fake giveaways, asking for money or passwords, fake sign-in pages.
rule_malicious_link_desc: Links to malware, phishing, or sites pretending to be other sites.
rule_illegal_goods_desc: Selling drugs, weapons, stolen accounts or exam answers.
rule_sexual_desc: Pornography and sexual acts, in images or text.
rule_gore_desc: Real images of severe injury or death posted to shock.
rule_copyright_desc: Reposting someone else’s paid work in full.
